Compensation Of Rs.2,37,700/- With Interest At 8% P.A.
From The Date Of Petition, Till Deposit.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. The insurer is in appeal challenging the finding of the Tribunal mainly contending that the Tribunal had committed an error in fastening the liability on it in the light of glaring evidence that the rider of the two wheeler who caused the accident did not have a driving licence and one Dayananda was implicated.

This stand taken by the insurer establishes that the occurrence of the accident involved the motor cycle is not in dispute and the only contention that is advanced is that the rider of the motor cycle was substituted.
2. In my view, even if this argument is to be accepted it would only amount to insurer putting forth the plea that there was a breach of policy conditions.
In such case the insurer would have to pay the compensation and thereafter recover from the owner of the offending vehicle.

3. In that view of the matter, I find no merit in this appeal and the appeal is dismissed.
4.

Liberty is, however, reserved to the insurer to proceed against the owner of the offending vehicle and establish that the rider of the motor cycle did not possess a valid Driving Licence as on the date of the accident and thereafter recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
5. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
